sections.h2: What kind of place is Bracken County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Bracken County is small and entirely rural, running along the Ohio River in the northern part of the state. Brooksville holds the courthouse, Augusta is the biggest town, and Germantown rounds out the three incorporated cities. Across the water lie Clermont and Brown counties in Ohio. On the Kentucky side the neighbors are Mason, Robertson, Harrison and Pendleton. Bracken falls inside the Cincinnati metro area, and it covers 209 square miles.

Kentucky made it the 23rd county in 1796 and named it for Big and Little Bracken creeks. The seat moved from Augusta to Woodward's Crossing, today's Brooksville, in 1833. White burley tobacco was bred from Bracken seed, and farm fields still define the landscape. The 2020 count was 8,400 residents, none of them in an urban area, and the July 2025 estimate stands at 8,511.

The Augusta area holds several Underground Railroad sites, because local abolitionists helped people cross the river to Ripley, Ohio, and Augusta College, founded in 1822, was the first Methodist college in the world.

When a value dispute arises, the sales records held at the PVA are what the county appeals board looks at.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about housing in Bracken County?
sections.html:
QuickFacts covers 2020 to 2024 for the figures below. Against Boyle, Breckinridge and Bullitt, Bracken has the cheapest typical home and the longest drive to work.

The 2020 count found 3,839 housing units, with 13.3 percent empty. Employers numbered 98 in 2023, and about 58.3 percent of residents 16 and older were in the labor force. Turnover is low: 95.7 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, the highest share of the four counties. The county counts 462 veterans, and broadband reaches 89.8 percent of households, and retail sales for 2022 totaled $29.6 million, or $3,506 per resident.

sections.h2: Who do I call about a Bracken County tax bill?
sections.html:
Valuing and collecting happen in separate offices that share the courthouse at 116 West Miami Street in Brooksville. The Property Valuation Administrator, 606-735-2228, owns the assessment, the property address, the name and mailing address on the bill, and exemptions. The Sheriff's Office (606-735-3233, second floor) only collects.

  • Address or name wrong: fix it on the return stub or call the PVA.
  • Disagree with the value: call the PVA before paying.
  • Bills from earlier years: County Clerk, 606-735-2952, on a separate check.

An online portal shows and takes payment for bills. Cards add a 2.50 percent charge that the cardholder pays and the sheriff does not keep. By mail, the check must cover the exact amount due.

sections.h2: When does the Bracken County discount end?
sections.html:
The sheriff gives the 2 percent discount period as October 1 through November 1. Bills go directly to owners. Later cutoffs and penalty steps are printed on the bill itself, and the sheriff's office can read them to you.

Escrow causes most of the grief. The sheriff mails to the owner and never to a mortgage company, so a borrower whose lender pays from escrow should pass the bill along as soon as it lands, or check that the lender has asked the sheriff for it. A check that bounces puts the bill back to unpaid, with the repayment schedule on the bill and a returned-check fee on top.

sections.h2: Why might a Bracken County bill carry the previous owner's name?
sections.html:
Ownership for tax purposes freezes on January 1. If a purchase closes after that, the bill for the year is addressed to the person who sold, and the PVA works from recorded deeds to find new owners. A buyer whose copy never turns up can ask the sheriff for one.

For a seller, that means a bill can show up at an address already left behind. The settlement agent normally divides the year by days of ownership and either pays the sheriff or credits whichever side will. Leave a forwarding address with the closing agent.

sections.h2: How does a Bracken County owner challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
Book a conference at the PVA first, since state rules require one before an appeal. The roll opens to inspection for thirteen days beginning with the first Monday of May, and appeals are filed with the clerk by the next workday after those days end.

If the PVA raises a value above what you listed, KRS 132.450(4) obliges the office to notify you. Anyone paid to speak for you must be an attorney, accountant, broker, appraiser or other qualified professional and must show your written authorization. Hearings may be recorded on audio.

sections.h2: What happens to an unpaid Bracken County bill after April 15?
sections.html:
The sheriff hands every unpaid bill to the County Clerk, who records a lien and files each as a certificate of delinquency. The clerk gives the Department of Revenue a list by May 15, and the Department publishes each county's list by June 1. On the normal schedule a tax sale can fall on any business day between July 14 and August 28.

Before that, the county attorney sends a 30-day letter and a second letter naming the sale date. The list is advertised in the paper with the biggest paid circulation between 30 and 45 days ahead and posted online at least 30 days ahead. An owner who still owes at the sale risks having the lien assigned to an outside buyer, who may add fees.

Interest accrues at 1 percent for every month or fraction. In the state's worked example, a $1,000 bill grows to $1,254 at transfer and to about $1,660 if paid after the June advertising.

sections.h2: Does Bracken County offer homestead relief?
sections.html:
Yes, to owners who turn 65 during the year or are permanently disabled. The Department of Revenue capped the exemption at $49,100 for tax years 2025 and 2026. The house must be your owned, occupied and maintained residence on January 1, and the application is due at the PVA by December 31.

The sheriff tells eligible owners to phone the PVA before paying a bill that lacks the exemption, because the exemption shrinks the bill. About 20.3 percent of Bracken residents are 65 or older.

sections.h2: How can I sell a Bracken County house that owes tax?
sections.html: Treat the tax as a closing item. Get the present balance from the sheriff and any older balance from the clerk, and have the closing agent pay both from the proceeds. Inherited houses, houses with tenants and houses that need more work than a retail buyer will take on often sell to cash buyers who accept the property as it stands and pay the tax at the table.

faqs.q: What is the Bracken County PVA's phone number?
faqs.a: 606-735-2228, at the courthouse in Brooksville. The office handles assessments, mailing addresses on bills and homestead exemptions.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Bracken County property tax bill?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's second-floor office in the courthouse, by mail, or through the sheriff's online portal. Card payments add 2.50 percent.

faqs.q: Does my mortgage company get my Bracken County tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff mails only to the owner. If your lender escrows taxes, forward the bill or ask the lender to request it.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a prior-year Bracken County bill?
faqs.a: At the County Clerk's office, 606-735-2952, with a separate check from the current year's payment.

faqs.q: Who owes tax on a Bracken County house sold in the spring?
faqs.a: The bill goes to whoever owned the house on January 1. Buyer and seller normally split the year at closing, and the agent pays the sheriff.
